subject: general
question: Pipe P can fill (2)/(9) part of a tank in 28 hours, and pipe Q can fill (2)/(7) part of the same tank in 12 hours. Both P and Q were kept open for 6 hours, then both were closed. Pipe R alone was then opened and it emptied the water in the tank in 8 hours. Pipes P, Q and R together can fill the empty tank in:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__
Time for **P** = 28 × (9/2) = 126 hrs; Time for **Q** = 12 × (7/2) = 42 hrs.

Work in 6 hrs = 6 × (1/126 + 1/42) = 6 × (1 + 3)/126 = 24/126 = 4/21 units.

**R** empties 4/21 units in 8 hrs → Full tank empty time = 8 × (21/4) = 42 hrs.

Combined Efficiency = 1/126 + 1/42 − 1/42 = 1/126.

**∴ The correct answer is 126 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Pipe **P** fills 2/9 part in 28 hrs.

Pipe **Q** fills 2/7 part in 12 hrs.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Full tank time for **P** = 28 × (9/2) = 126 hours.

⇒ Full tank time for **Q** = 12 × (7/2) = 42 hours.

 **Person** **Days** **Total Work** **Efficiency**
 **P** 126 126 1
 **Q** 42 3
⇒ Work done by **P** and **Q** in 6 hours = 6 × (1 + 3) = 24 units.

⇒ Pipe **R** empties 24 units in 8 hours.

⇒ Efficiency of **R** = 24 ÷ 8 = 3 units/hr (negative work).

⇒ Combined Efficiency (**P + Q + R**) = 1 + 3 − 3 = 1 unit/hr.

⇒ Time taken by all three = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency = 126 ÷ 1 = 126 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 126 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inlet and Outlet Pipes

Inlet pipes add water (positive efficiency) while outlet pipes remove water (negative efficiency).

Fractional Work Formula

If 1/n part is done in t hours, total time T = n × t.</p
